page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Eadsv7 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 945 GB disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both rank in the top 10% of tested servers, alongside top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests, such as large-block read and write operations, also perform within the average range. For language model tasks, text generation using a small 135M model is strong, while prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core and the inclusion of a 945 GB local disk, this server provides high resource density for memory-intensive workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, in-memory caching, text processing, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing power and substantial RAM capacity makes it a viable option for workloads requiring large memory footprints without requiring a high vCPU count.

Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. With 16.0 GB of memory per core and Premium Storage capability, this server is designed for memory-intensive applications, text processing, and database workloads that benefit from a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local storage without requiring massive multi-core compute scaling.
